pillars.p: Thermal degradation, ASTM E595 outgassing, and vacuum exposure of aerospace polymers. Which materials survive, how fast they change, and what that means for a mission lifetime.
Root-cause and non-destructive evaluation of CFRP, plus thermoplastic processing and rheology on PEEK, PAEK, PBI, PTFE, and PI systems.
Machine learning applied to polymer characterization data, so property prediction doesn't stall at the throughput of one person reading spectra.

ps: The labs I want to join build ultra-thin composite structures that fold, deploy, and hold their shape in orbit. The mechanics of those structures are well studied. The materials question underneath them is less settled: how a polymer matrix behaves after months of thermal cycling and vacuum, and how you choose the right system for a specific mission instead of a generic one.

That's the half I've worked on. At NASA Glenn I characterized degradation in aerospace polymer systems and built the testing and documentation procedure that made the results usable by people who aren't materials engineers. On the Boeing spoiler project I ran root-cause and NDT work on carbon fiber laminates. I'd like to bring that to a structures group.
